options.text: The SCP permits delegation of S3 actions but does not grant them to the IAM user. The user still needs an applicable IAM permission for s3:CreateBucket.
OU-attached SCPs are not inherited by member accounts until the same policy is separately attached to every account.
The Resource value must contain the new bucket ARN; an SCP using an asterisk cannot permit bucket creation.
An SCP with S3 allow statements authorizes only the member-account root user, so ordinary IAM users cannot receive S3 permissions.

explanation.text:
<<1>> is correct. The organization guardrail allows the action to be granted, but the described user has no identity permission that grants it. Add only the required IAM permissions within the allowed scope.

<<2>> denies the inheritance that OU policies provide. The account does not need a duplicate attachment merely to inherit the OU restriction.

<<3>> invents a requirement for a bucket-specific SCP resource. The shown wildcard does not cause the missing IAM grant.

<<4>> misstates SCP scope. SCPs can limit member-account IAM users and roles as well as root activity within their documented scope; they are not grants reserved for root.

Evaluate the organization ceiling and the actual access grant separately. The stem explicitly establishes permits at every ancestor and the account level. Leaving FullAWSAccess beside this allowlist at the same OU would broaden that level's permitted actions rather than enforcing an EC2-and-S3-only ceiling.

Official AWS references (checked September 18, 2026): [SCPs do not grant access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html). [SCP evaluation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html).
